publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

operator-walkthrough.ref:
WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — nothing on Instagram, which is how this was found. The operator asked why autonomous reels had stopped; production said the rest.  ★ ONE — A BILLING WALL FILED AS A TRANSIENT BLIP. Reel job #1380001 (2026-08-04 18:03, cron) failed with Higgsfield's grace_daily_limit_reached / unlock_full_access_notice. That text matched NONE of the eight classifier patterns — no "billing", no "exhausted", and no "rate" for RATE_LIMIT — so it fell through to UNKNOWN, whose policy is RETRY_BACKOFF and whose operator-facing reason literally reads "unrecognised failure - treated as transient, but review the message". The daily cron re-attempted every day and NOTHING alerted. It now classifies as QUOTA_OR_CREDIT -> PAUSE_PROVIDER, which stops the lane and raises a human.  Deliberately NOT RATE_LIMIT, and the difference is money: RATE_LIMIT is RETRY_WITHOUT_CONSUMING_ATTEMPT, built for a request refused before work began that clears on its own. A grace-tier daily cap does not clear by waiting and cannot be retried out of - it needs a plan upgrade. A test asserts it is not that class.  ★ THE TEST CAUGHT A TRAP IN MY OWN FIX. The first draft appended the new wordings to the existing QUOTA_OR_CREDIT regex, which is wrapped in  ... . `_` is a WORD character, so   never fires inside an underscore-joined token:  grace[_ ]daily[_ ]limit  does NOT match "grace_daily_limit_reached", because the boundary it wants sits between `limit` and `_reached` with word characters on both sides. Three cases went red. The plan-wall patterns are now their own entry and the working credit regex is untouched.  ★ TWO — A TRUNCATED RESPONSE REPORTED AS A BACKTICK. ig_autopost_log carried `Unexpected token '`', "```json
{"... is not valid JSON` (2026-08-05) and `Unterminated string in JSON at position 830` (2026-08-01). Both are ONE root cause - the model's output was cut off mid-object - and neither message says so; the first names the backtick, which is the only detail that does not matter. parseJsonObject now detects an opening brace with no closing one and throws `LLM response truncated before the JSON object closed (N chars received) - raise max_tokens for this call`, and wraps genuine syntax errors instead of leaking the raw parser text into a column the operator reads.  ★ AND A MUTATION PROVED PART OF MY OWN FIX DEAD. The draft also stripped an UNCLOSED fence. Disabling that line changed no behaviour: the brace isolation already recovers the object whenever one closed, and when none closed the truncation branch fires first either way. It was removed rather than kept with a comment claiming it fixed the prod error. The surviving branch is verified load-bearing - disabling it turns 2 cases red.  EVIDENCE: server/providerErrorAndLlmJsonTruth.test.ts (10), built from the EXACT prod stderr payload rather than a paraphrase, MUTATION-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS - removing the plan-wall pattern (3 red) · reclassifying it as RATE_LIMIT (4 red) · disabling the truncation branch (2 red) · deleting the truncation message (1 red). One further mutation SURVIVED and that is why a line was deleted; the first attempt at it silently failed to apply and reported a false pass, so the applied ones are proven by echoing the removed text and by git diff --stat. A regression case pins that the other six error classes are unchanged. Full serial suite: 405 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,981 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean.  NOT CLAIMED: neither fix makes a reel. The Higgsfield account is behind a plan-tier daily cap - an operator billing action - and this change only makes that state stop the lane loudly instead of retrying it silently. No production run has exercised either path since the change; the classification is asserted against the recorded payload, not against a new live failure.

The rule fires on server/services/loopShapeContract.ts, where the ONLY changes are comments plus dropping expectedRunsPerWeek from the cross_sell contract entry - recording that the loop is deliberately unscheduled (ROS-033, operator decision 2026-08-04: retire). render-spend-trajectory.ref: NO SPEND CHANGES IN THIS DIFF, and that is the claim being made rather than dodged. The rule fires because services/higgsfieldStudio.ts is touched, so here is exactly what was touched in it.  materializeStartImage's inline SSRF guard and bounded-read loop were EXTRACTED to lib/publicFetch.ts and are now called instead of inlined — 126 lines removed, zero rules changed. The extraction is byte-faithful: the same CIDR-parsed IPv4 blocks, the same IPv4-inside-IPv6 handling, the same FQDN-root-dot strip, the same per-hop revalidation, the same START_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES cap and START_IMAGE_MAX_REDIRECTS limit passed in as options. The now-unused `isIP` import was dropped.  Nothing on the generation or billing path is touched. No reservation is created, settled or released differently; reelClipCostUsd, COST_ESTIMATES_USD, reelLedgerModel and every reserve/settle call site are untouched by this diff. materializeStartImage is a DOWNLOAD of an already-generated frame — it makes no provider call and books no cost — and its failure contract is unchanged: every failure still returns null and the clip renders text-only, because conditioning is an enhancement that must degrade a reel rather than break it.  The only behavioural difference is which module the same refusals come from, which is why the check that matters is the existing suite rather than a new spend assertion: higgsfieldStudio's 53 tests pass unchanged, and the extracted rules gained 17 of their own in server/publicFetch.test.ts (they previously had none of their own — they were reachable only through materializeStartImage).  Full serial suite: 394 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,879 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean. NOT CLAIMED: no live spend trajectory, no provider call, no production render — nothing here was measured against generation_reservations.
